summary: Tehama County tower with a 1963 steel cab on a lookout site used since at least 1933; CAL FIRE site, NHLR-registered 2019; last staffing listed 2008.

facts.design: Steel cab based on USFS design CL-30 on a USFS 1600-series tower; earlier BC-301 cab on an enclosed timber tower

access.note: Site is 2.7 miles from the nearest paved road (NHLR); CAL FIRE does not rent lookouts (2008 CAL FIRE list)

facts.agency: California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection - Tehama-Glenn Unit (Cal Fire TGU)

events.note: Earliest known lookout structure here, an open platform, per NHLR: 'since at least 1933'
October 14, 1938 item: station known locally as Pigeon Roost, because wandering homing pigeons favored it
Current tower and steel cab; the year is written on the northwest pier
Smoke from a 100-acre grass fire west of Henleyville was spotted from the lookout (Red Bluff Daily News item of July 27, 1971, reprinted)
California Department of Forestry took over the site
Lower room added 'ten years later' than the 1972 takeover; the year is derived from that phrase; the story says about a decade later
June 2008 CAL FIRE list names lookouts that may be staffed in the 2008 fire season, including Eagle Peak

notes_for_editor: The newest staffing record is the June 2008 CAL FIRE list, and the newest registry event is 2019; current condition, staffing and public access are unverified. The 1982 lower-room date is derived from 'ten years later'. The 1971 fire item is a reprint of a Red Bluff Daily News story. The CAL FIRE PDF is a copy on a personal site (citlink.net), not a CAL FIRE URL. The brief's 1963 build date is the current tower; a lookout has stood here since at least 1933.
